language.bannerText: Esta web también está disponible en español.
footer.summary: An environment for learning to program in pseudocode, with step-by-step execution and diagrams drawn by the language engine itself.
home.seoTitle: PseudoLearn · Learn to program by watching what your program does
home.seoDescription: Pseudocode editor for macOS and iOS: run step by step and keep the code, the flowchart, the structogram and the trace table in sync. A 15-module path with 95 exercises.
home.hero.title: Programming clicks when you can see it.
home.hero.lead: PseudoLearn runs your pseudocode one statement at a time and keeps the same step highlighted in the code, the flowchart, the structogram and the trace table. Behind it sits a 15-module path with 95 self-checking exercises.
home.hero.requirements: macOS 13 or later · Apple Silicon and Intel · iOS 16 or later · Works offline
home.preview.alt: PseudoLearn with the GuidedDemo program already run: the source code, its matching flowchart and the three lines the program printed.
home.preview.caption: The same statement is marked in the code and in the flowchart. On a phone the two panels stack; on a desktop they share the width.
home.platforms.label: Availability
home.surfaces.title: One step, four surfaces, no mental leap.
home.surfaces.lead: Almost nobody learns to program by reading a flowchart drawn by hand on a separate sheet. In PseudoLearn the four surfaces are projections of the same program, generated by the engine: when the interpreter advances, the highlight moves in all of them at once. There is also a UML class diagram when the program uses objects.
home.surfaces.code.title: Code
home.surfaces.code.subtitle: Statement in progress
home.surfaces.code.caption: The statement being executed gets its own background and its number lights up in the gutter, with no cursor to hunt for.
home.surfaces.flowchart.title: Flowchart
home.surfaces.flowchart.subtitle: Active node
home.surfaces.flowchart.caption: Drawn by the engine from the syntax tree: the shape says what the node does and the loop return uses the brand colour.
home.surfaces.flowchart.diagramLabel: Flowchart of a While loop: the condition diamond exits through the YES branch into the active assignment node, and the loop return comes back to the diamond from the left.
home.surfaces.structogram.title: Structogram
home.surfaces.structogram.subtitle: Visible nesting
home.surfaces.structogram.caption: Nassi-Shneiderman: no arrows and no jumps, the block structure is the box itself.
home.surfaces.trace.title: Trace table
home.surfaces.trace.subtitle: One row per step
home.surfaces.trace.caption: The table your teacher asks you to fill in by hand, filled in by the interpreter. With object identity and aliasing when there are any.
home.surfaces.trace.tableLabel: Trace table for the example loop
home.track.title: It is not a pile of tutorials. It is a path with an order.
home.track.lead: Fifteen modules across three stages, written to be read in that order. Each module explains one idea, shows it running and closes with exercises the app checks against visible and hidden cases.
home.track.diagramLabel: The PseudoLearn symbol path, stretched horizontally: a start node, three stepped stages and the finish flag
home.track.stageA.label: STAGE A
home.track.stageB.label: STAGE B
home.track.stageC.label: STAGE C
home.track.stageA.title: Foundations
home.track.stageB.title: Structured programming
home.track.stageC.title: Objects
home.track.stageA.summary: Before writing anything: what a sequence of steps must satisfy to be called an algorithm, and the notional machine you will reason with for the rest of the path.
home.track.stageB.summary: The bulk of the path: data, decisions, the three loops and when each one applies, arrays, subprograms and recursion. It closes by reading programs from their diagram.
home.track.stageC.summary: From loose variables to a thing with state and behaviour. It includes the point where almost everyone gets lost: identity, aliasing and what really happens when you copy an object.
home.track.footer: No grades, no achievement percentages and no attempt history that follows you around. An exercise is checked and tells you what is missing; none of it turns into a mark.
home.features.overline: Why this and not a notebook
home.features.title: Six things paper cannot do.
home.features.stepping.title: Step-by-step execution, at four speeds
home.features.stepping.description: The interpreter advances one statement at a time and you choose the speed. The focus moves at once in the code, the diagrams and the trace table, so you never have to guess where you are.
home.features.diagnostics.title: Errors that explain rather than scold
home.features.diagnostics.description: Every diagnostic marks its exact span and the related spans too — the missing declaration, the extra EndWhile — as you type, not at the end.
home.features.projection.title: From pseudocode to Python and Rust
home.features.projection.description: The equivalent-code tab projects your program into two industrial languages, line by line, so you can see the correspondence before making the jump to one of them.
home.features.objects.title: Objects stop being magic
home.features.objects.description: The trace table shows the identity of each instance (Account#1) and does not collapse aliases. Seeing two names pointing at the same object settles in one step what a paragraph cannot.
home.features.ownership.title: Your programs are your files
home.features.ownership.description: They are saved as .pseudo plain text, on your disk. The app works fully offline; the account and sync are optional, not an entry toll.
home.features.bilingual.title: In Spanish and English, not half-translated
home.features.bilingual.description: The reserved words, the knowledge base, the exercises and the diagnostics all exist in both languages. Switching language changes the language, not just the buttons.
home.downloads.title: Install it where you study.
home.downloads.mobileInput: Key bar with the language keywords
home.downloads.upcomingText: Windows, Linux and Android. No announced date: they will be published here when they are ready, not before.
home.closing.title: Start with Stage A. It is two modules.
home.closing.lead: By the time you finish the second one you will have run an algorithm step by step and read its trace table. From there, the rest of the path makes sense.
home.closing.note: Also on the App Store for iPhone and iPad
contact.seoDescription: Write to report a bug, propose a feature, suggest an improvement or settle a question about PseudoLearn. The same person who writes the code reads it.
contact.hero.title: Tell me what is missing, what is broken or what does not make sense.
contact.hero.lead: There is no suggestion box here that nobody opens. The same person who writes the code reads it, and a feature you miss weighs as much as a bug. It may take a few days to reply, but it replies.
contact.form.title: What do you want to tell me about?
contact.form.note: Pick one and the questions adjust. Fields marked with an asterisk are required.
contact.reason.error.title: Something is broken
contact.reason.error.description: A bug, an odd result, something that crashes.
contact.reason.feature.title: Something is missing
contact.reason.feature.description: A feature you need that is not there.
contact.reason.improvement.title: It could be better
contact.reason.question.title: I have a question
contact.reason.question.description: About the language, a module or the app.
contact.branch.error.label: So it can be reproduced
contact.branch.error.snippetLabel: Paste the program that triggers it here
contact.branch.error.snippetPlaceholder: Paste the contents of your .pseudo file. It is what shortens the fix the most.
contact.branch.error.snippetHelp: Plain text, up to 4000 characters. No attachments needed.
contact.branch.feature.label: Before the idea, the problem
contact.branch.feature.intro: If you tell me the feature you want, I build that feature. If you tell me what you wanted it for, sometimes there is a better solution neither of us had thought of.
contact.branch.feature.intentLabel: What were you trying to do when you missed it? *
contact.branch.feature.intentPlaceholder: Compare two versions of the same algorithm
contact.branch.feature.workaroundLabel: What do you do instead right now?
contact.branch.feature.workaroundPlaceho: I duplicate the document and open two windows
contact.branch.feature.workaroundHelp: The workaround you already use says more than any description: if there is none, maybe it was not needed.
contact.branch.improvement.label: Where the friction is
contact.branch.improvement.areaHelp: Editor · Flowchart · Structogram · Class diagram · Trace table · Knowledge base · Library · Settings
contact.branch.improvement.frictionLabel: What took more effort than it should?
contact.branch.improvement.frictionPlace: Finding the object column among so many
contact.branch.question.label: About what
contact.branch.question.generalOption: Another question about the language or the app
contact.branch.question.subjectHelp: The 15 path modules and the 11 specification documents.
contact.branch.question.notice: That module’s specification is already inside the app, offline. Check it first in case it saves you the wait.
contact.field.messageLabel: Tell me in your own words *
contact.field.messagePlaceholder: I would like to have two programs open at once to compare how the trace table changes between a recursive one and an iterative one.
contact.hint.error: Paste the program that triggers it and what you expected to happen.
contact.hint.feature: You do not need to propose how it should work: the problem is enough.
contact.hint.improvement: Describe the exact moment you got stuck, not the app in general.
contact.hint.question: The more specific the question, the shorter and more useful the answer.
contact.checkbox.telemetry: Attach the app version and the operating system.
contact.checkbox.telemetrySubtext: Your code and documents are not sent.
contact.checkbox.privacy: I have read how my data is handled *
contact.submit.question: Send the question
contact.submit.copyNote: You will receive a copy by email.

contact.status.mailFailed: Delivery failed on our side. Write directly to the support address.

contact.error.emailInvalid: Enter a valid email address so I can reply.

contact.sidebar.promisesLabel: What happens to what you send
contact.sidebar.promiseHuman: A person reads it, not an automatic classifier.
contact.sidebar.promiseReply: I always reply, even when the answer is no.
contact.sidebar.promiseNoGuarantee: I do not promise to build what you ask for. I promise to read it and tell you why or why not.
contact.sidebar.responseTimeNote: If it passes and you have nothing, send it again: it will have been lost.
contact.sidebar.tipContext: What you were doing at that moment.
contact.sidebar.tipActual: What happened instead, or what you were missing.
contact.sidebar.emailNote: It is the same inbox the form reaches. If you prefer your mail client, use this one.
contact.sidebar.knowledgeText: The app’s knowledge base ships 15 modules and 11 language specification documents. Many syntax questions are settled there without waiting for a reply.
module.CON-B1: B1 · Data: types, variables, expressions and assignment
module.CON-B4: B4 · Iteration: the three loops and when each applies
module.CON-B5: B5 · Arrays: one dimension and two
module.CON-B6: B6 · Decomposition: procedures, functions, parameters and scope
module.CON-B8: B8 · Reading a program: flowchart and structogram
module.CON-C1: C1 · Why objects: from variables to classes
module.CON-C2: C2 · Class: attributes, visibility, methods and constructor
module.CON-C5: C5 · Design: who owns each responsibility
versions.seoDescription: Which version of PseudoLearn is released, what new features it includes and the detailed changelog.
versions.hero.title: Release history and updates.
versions.hero.lead: Browse all published versions of PseudoLearn, their new features, and the detailed changelog. No entry on this page says “performance improvements and bug fixes”.
versions.current.title: Right now there is a single version.
versions.current.lead: The same one for everybody. There is no test channel, no paid edition and no feature that depends on having chipped in.
versions.current.requirements: macOS 13 or later · iOS 16 or iPadOS 16 and later · Apple Silicon and Intel · Works offline
versions.history.title: Everything that has been released.
versions.history.lead: One entry per version, newest first, with all features, improvements, and changes detailed in depth.
versions.history.floorText: {version} is the first released version, and that is information too: whatever came before never reached a store or a student.
versions.release.1-0-0.headline: First stable version
versions.release.1-0-0.summary: It ships complete: the whole language, the four synchronized surfaces and the learning track end to end. It is not a preview and it is not early access.
versions.release.1-0-0.languageText: Imperative, structured and object-oriented programming: primitive types, decisions, the three loops, arrays, subprograms, recursion, classes, inheritance and polymorphism.
versions.release.1-0-0.executionText: The interpreter advances one statement at a time, at four paces, with diagnostics that point at their exact span while you type.
versions.release.1-0-0.diagramsText: Flowchart, structogram and desk-check table, drawn by the engine and highlighted along with the code. UML class diagram when the program uses objects.
versions.release.1-0-0.projectionText: Line-by-line projection of your program into Python and Rust.
versions.release.1-0-0.trackText: Three stages, 15 modules and 95 exercises that check themselves, with the language knowledge base alongside.
versions.release.1-0-0.filesText: Plain-text .pseudo programs saved on your own disk. The app works entirely offline.
versions.release.1-0-0.accountText: Optional. Turn it on and your documents follow you between the Mac, the iPhone and the iPad; leave it off and the app asks you for nothing.
versions.release.1-0-0.appText: macOS 13, iOS 16 and iPadOS 16 or later, in Spanish and English, with a light and a dark theme.
versions.report.title: Did something that worked yesterday stop working?
versions.report.text: Tell us the app version and the program triggering the issue. With those details and a reproducible case, a bug is fixed in an afternoon; described from memory it may never be fixed.

privacy.seoDescription: How we handle your data in PseudoLearn: fully functional without an account, local storage, and zero analytics or advertising.
privacy.hero.title: Your code stays on your device.
privacy.hero.lead: PseudoLearn works completely without an account. If you do not sign in, your algorithms and progress never leave your machine: no server ever receives them.
privacy.summary.title: Executive summary
privacy.summary.lead: Our privacy policy rests upon three core principles that guide the design of the application:
privacy.summary.pillar1Text: The app is 100% functional without signing in. Neither your code nor your progress ever leaves your computer.
privacy.summary.pillar2Text: Your algorithms are saved as plain .pseudo text files on your own disk.
privacy.summary.pillar3Text: No behavioral telemetry, no advertising, no data sales, and no training AI models with your code.
privacy.toc.title: On this page
privacy.nav.supportText: If you have any questions regarding your data or wish to exercise your rights, write to us directly:
privacy.section.data.title: Data we process
privacy.section.data.lead: The volume of information we process depends strictly on how you choose to use PseudoLearn.
privacy.section.data.cardNoAccountTitle: If you use the app without an account: none
privacy.section.data.cardNoAccountText: The algorithms you write, your progress through the knowledge base, and your preferences are kept solely within the app directory on your device. We have no access to them and no technical means of recovering them.
privacy.section.data.cardAccountTitle: If you choose to sign in (optional)
privacy.section.data.cardAccountText: An account only enables backup and synchronization across your devices. It stores your user identifier, email address, display name or photo if provided by your login provider, algorithm metadata and contents, completed modules, and general preferences.
privacy.section.data.cardContactTitle: If you contact us via the web form
privacy.section.data.cardContactText: We process your contact reason, email, message, and any program snippet you voluntarily paste. Your browser environment telemetry is only transmitted if you check the corresponding box, and your IP address is sent to the anti-bot service solely to verify you are human.
privacy.section.data.calloutTitle: What we do not do by product decision
privacy.section.data.calloutText: We do not implement usage analytics, behavioral telemetry, advertising, or user profiling. We do not track how long it takes you to solve an exercise or rank you against other learners. We never sell data to third parties, and we never use your code to train artificial intelligence models.
privacy.section.storage.title: Where data is stored
privacy.section.storage.lead: Your data resides primarily on your local machine and, secondarily and encrypted, in European infrastructure.
privacy.section.storage.deviceText: Your programs are always saved as plain-text .pseudo files alongside a local index. That is the primary, self-contained copy, whether you have an account or not.
privacy.section.storage.cloudText: Only if you chose to sign in. Supabase is our authentication and database provider. All data travels encrypted over HTTPS/TLS, and the backend enforces Row-Level Security (RLS) so each account can only access its own records. Session tokens are stored securely in your system Keychain.
privacy.section.storage.webText: The website runs on Cloudflare Workers and does not retain databases of form submissions. The contact form generates a secure email dispatched through Oracle Cloud (Frankfurt) directly to our support inbox.
privacy.section.storage.assetsText: The website does not request fonts or scripts from third-party hosts to ensure your IP address is not shared. Only your theme and language choices are stored locally, which is why you will never see cookie consent banners or trackers.
privacy.section.auth.title: Account access and age requirements
privacy.section.auth.lead: Authentication is handled through established identity providers or direct magic links.
privacy.section.auth.providersText: You can sign in with Apple, Google, or a magic link sent to your email. If you use Sign in with Apple and conceal your address, we receive Apple private relay address and never your real inbox.
privacy.section.auth.ageText: Creating an account requires being at least 16 years of age or the legal minimum in your country with parental consent. However, the app can be used without an account at any age with complete safety.
privacy.section.deletion.title: Deleting your account and data
privacy.section.deletion.lead: We guarantee the right to permanent deletion directly and without bureaucratic hurdles.
privacy.section.deletion.selfServiceText: You can delete your account at any time via Settings → Account → Delete account. Upon confirmation, your cloud account, synced algorithms, learning progress, and cloud preferences are permanently and immediately purged.
privacy.section.deletion.localRetentionT: Deleting your account does not remove algorithms saved locally on your machine to prevent accidental data loss. When signing out, you can choose whether to keep or remove local files.
privacy.section.deletion.manualText: You may also request account deletion by emailing support@pseudolearn.com from your registered address. Requests are processed within 30 days, with backup snapshots rotating within a maximum 30-day window.
privacy.section.retention.title: Retention periods
privacy.section.retention.lead: We adhere to strict data minimization and finite retention periods.
privacy.section.retention.itemDevice: Local files on your device: kept until you delete them or uninstall the application.
privacy.section.retention.itemSync: Synchronized records: for the lifetime of your active account. Deleted algorithms retain a 90-day technical tombstone marker solely to propagate deletion to other devices.
privacy.section.retention.itemSupport: Support communications: kept for 24 months from the last reply to ensure continuity in issue resolution.
privacy.section.retention.itemInactivity: Inactive accounts: if an account remains unused for 24 months, an email notification will precede its automatic deletion.
privacy.section.rights.title: Your rights
privacy.section.rights.lead: We uphold rigorous international standards for personal data protection.
privacy.section.rights.text1: You have the right to access, rectify, cancel, and oppose the processing of your personal data (ARCO rights under Peru Law No. 29733, as well as rights of erasure, restriction, and data portability under the GDPR in the EU and the CCPA in California).
privacy.section.rights.text2: Your files belong to you: you can export all your algorithms in plain text at any time directly from the app. For additional requests, email us at support@pseudolearn.com (response within 30 days).
privacy.section.rights.text3: We do not sell or share personal information with commercial advertisers, meaning no opt-out configuration is ever required.
privacy.section.contact.title: Changes and contact
privacy.section.contact.lead: We maintain full transparency with our community regarding policy updates.
privacy.section.contact.text1: Any future updates to this policy will appear on this page along with an updated effective date. If a change is material and you hold an active account, we will notify you by email.
privacy.section.contact.text2: For any inquiries regarding your privacy, contact us at support@pseudolearn.com. You will receive a direct, personal response from the creator of the project.

terms.summary.title: Summary of terms

terms.summary.pillar2Text: No sign-up or personal data submission is needed to study or use the platform.
terms.summary.pillar3Text: Zero hidden subscriptions and no unauthorized third-party billing gateways outside official app stores.

terms.section.acceptance.text: By downloading, installing, or using PseudoLearn, you accept these terms. If you disagree with any portion, you must refrain from using the software. terms.section.ip.coreText: The source code of the language engine and native applications is closed-source and our proprietary property.
terms.section.ip.curriculumText: The 15 learning modules, language specifications, and exercise sets are protected by copyright. terms.section.pricing.title: Pricing and purchases

terms.section.pricing.text2: The website stores no payment information, includes no third-party payment gateways, and accepts no donations or direct payments.
terms.section.availability.title: Availability and offline-first design
terms.section.availability.lead: Network independence to safeguard your learning progress.
terms.section.availability.text1: All core functions of PseudoLearn — the editor, code parser, step-by-step interpreter, interactive diagrams, and exercises — operate 100% offline without an internet connection.
terms.section.availability.text2: Cloud synchronization is provided as-is subject to infrastructure availability. In the unlikely event that sync services are discontinued, at least 30 days notice will be provided to export your data without impacting local storage.

terms.section.privacy.text: The handling of your personal data is detailed comprehensively in our Privacy Policy, which forms a binding part of these terms.
terms.section.governing.title: Governing law and contact
terms.section.governing.text1: These terms are governed by the laws of the Republic of Peru, while fully respecting consumer protection statutes applicable in your jurisdiction of residence.
terms.section.governing.text2: For any questions regarding these terms, contact us at support@pseudolearn.com. You will receive direct assistance from the creator of the software.
